cat -n src/api.ts; grep -rn "id" src/git-auth.ts src/dashboard.ts src/tasks.ts src/untracked.ts | head -50; grep -rn "buildRoutes\|registerRepo\|cacheListing\|template\|validate\|sanitiz" src
input.description: Show api.ts and search for route wiring and validation

input.reason: Both findings are confirmed after edits. In src/routes.ts, registerRepo (lines 18-23) only rejects an empty id. It then stores the id (line 21) and passes it to cloneRepo (line 22), which uses it as a directory through cachePath. The code does not validate ids anywhere: api.ts, store.ts, worktree.ts and config.ts have no validation, and the repository has no tests. The template route (line 36) builds its base directory with path.join(REPOS_DIR, req.params.id). Its startsWith check on line 38 only compares against that base, which may already sit outside REPOS_DIR, so the check does not stop the escape. cacheListing (line 60) calls cachePath, which is path.resolve(REPOS_DIR, id) (worktree.ts:10). With `../../etc`, both routes resolve outside /var/harbor/repos. With `/etc`, only path.resolve escapes; path.join produces /var/harbor/repos/etc. So F12's claim about absolute paths had to be limited to the cache listing route. F14's claim that the base directory comes from the raw id holds. Its CLAUDE.md rule is not supported, because the working tree has no CLAUDE.md: it holds only package.json and src/.
input.summary: Unvalidated repository ids let template and cache routes escape REPOS_DIR

findings.text: The repository id is stored with no character or path validation and later used as a directory name. An id such as `../../etc` escapes the repositories directory on both the template route and the cache listing route, and an absolute path such as `/etc` escapes it on the cache listing route.
findings.reason: Line 20 only checks that the id is present, and line 21 stores it as given. Line 22 then uses it as a directory through cloneRepo, which calls cachePath. `../../etc` escapes on both routes: path.join and path.resolve both turn it into /var/etc. An absolute id escapes only on the cache listing route. cachePath uses path.resolve, so `/etc` becomes /etc. The template route uses path.join, which treats `/etc` as a normal segment and gives /var/harbor/repos/etc, still inside the repositories directory. The sentence was changed so the absolute-path escape applies only to the cache listing route.

findings.text: The template route builds its base directory from the raw repository id.
findings.reason: The main claim holds. Line 36 joins REPOS_DIR with req.params.id and does no validation first. The check on line 38 only confirms the file is under that base, so a traversing id still gets through. The second sentence cites a CLAUDE.md rule, but there is no CLAUDE.md in the working tree (only package.json and src/), so nothing supports it. That sentence was removed.

input.severity_reason: This is a path traversal flaw that can be exploited. On the template route, an id like `../../..` makes the base `/`, so the line 38 check passes for any path in the name parameter, which allows reading arbitrary files. cacheListing can read any file named INDEX. registerRepo can make git clone into a directory outside REPOS_DIR. None of these routes validates the id.
